questions.prompt: What does the phloem carry through a plant?
questions.explanation: Phloem carries the food (sugar) that the leaves make through photosynthesis to the rest of the plant.
questions.misconception: Phloem is not the water-pipe or a seed part - it is the food tissue that moves the sugar made in leaves to other parts.

questions.prompt: Where does the food in the phloem start, and where does it go?
options: It starts in the leaves and goes out to the whole plant
It starts in the roots and goes to the leaves
It goes only to the sun
questions.explanation: The sugar food is made in the leaves and carried by the phloem to roots, fruits, seeds, and growing shoots all over the plant.
questions.misconception: Phloem food does not start in the roots and then rise - it is made in the leaves and delivered outward to where the plant needs it.

questions.prompt: What is unusual about phloem tubes compared to water pipes?
options: They are made of living cells that help move the food
They are made of hard rock
questions.explanation: Phloem is made of living cells that actively help move the sugar, unlike xylem which is more like simple pipes.
questions.misconception: Unlike a plain pipe or a rock tube, a phloem tube is a living structure that works to push the food along.

questions.prompt: Which parts of a plant receive the food delivered by the phloem?
options: Roots, seeds, fruits, and growing shoots
questions.explanation: The phloem delivers food to roots, seeds, fruits, and growing shoots so every living part of the plant stays fed.
questions.misconception: The phloem does not just feed one leaf; it shares the leaves' food with the roots, seeds, and fruits across the plant.
